meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Thank you for seeing me. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Start there.
Okay. Don't thank me yet. Sit down, and tell me what's on the gradebook and when it went in.
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me. I've done this for twenty years. Owen's essay is what we're here about, so tell me what you have on it.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
I'm not answering questions about Owen's life from a teacher who hasn't shown me a single document about his essay. Show me what you have, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
So it's at least possible he used it once?
No. I'm not answering a hypothetical about my son. You've told me a score and a feeling. What else do you have?
I agree that anything is possible, and that isn't evidence. Put the zero in front of me with a date on it, or tell me you don't have one.
